extracted.intended_audience: HHS rulemaking commenters, health insurers/issuers, state regulators, Treasury/IRS staff, and policy analysts involved in ACA payment parameter setting
extracted.subtask_description: Establishes the methodology and numerical parameters (premium adjustment percentage, maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, reduced limits, required contribution percentage) for ACA plan year 2026 and describes how HHS will calculate, round, publish, and justify those values. Includes both substantive selection criteria and procedural calculation rules to guide the choice of premium measure and downstream parameter setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The premium adjustment percentage should be calculated based on the average per capita premium for health insurance coverage for the entire market, including the individual and group markets, and both fully insured and self-insured group health plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS has previously used this as a primary criterion (2015 Payment Notice). Deviations from comprehensiveness should be justified (e.g., temporary instability in a market segment). The proposed PY 2026 measure returns to a market-comprehensive approach (private health insurance excluding Medigap and property and casualty insurance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The data underlying the calculation should be available by the summer of the year that is prior to the calendar year so that the premium adjustment percentage can be published in the annual HHS notice of benefit and payment parameters in time for issuers to develop their plan designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS requires timely availability of source data (e.g., NHEA estimates/projections) to publish parameters by the required schedule. Availability was one of four criteria used in prior notices (2015, 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The methodology for estimating the average premium should be easily understandable and predictable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS favors methods whose calculations and inputs are clear and explainable to stakeholders. When methodology changes are proposed, transparency includes publishing rationale and calculation steps in notices and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The methodology should have a record of accurately estimating average premiums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS weighs whether a measure historically tracks true premium growth and avoids volatility that would misestimate long-term premium trends. Accuracy concerns motivated past reliance on ESI-only measures during times of individual market instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium measure to use (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: For PY 2026 and beyond, calculate the premium adjustment percentage using an adjusted private individual and group market health insurance premium measure similar to NHEA's private health insurance premium measure (including ESI and direct purchase) but excluding Medigap and property and casualty insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHEA's private health insurance premium includes ESI, direct purchase (on- and off-Exchange), Medigap, and medical portion of accident/property and casualty. The proposed HHS measure uses NHEA estimates/projections of ESI and direct purchase but excludes Medigap and property and casualty, consistent with the 2020 Payment Notice approach. Rationale: these exclusions focus on primary medical coverage and align comprehensiveness and accuracy criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude Medigap and property & casualty from numerator and denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: Medigap and property and casualty insurance premiums should be excluded from the premium measure and the count of enrollees (denominator) when calculating average per-enrollee premiums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Medigap supplements Original Medicare and property and casualty insurance's medical portions are not primary medical coverage for individuals electing enrollment. Specifically, calculate 2013 and 2025 measures as private health insurance premiums minus premiums paid for Medigap and property and casualty insurance, divided by the unrounded number of unique private health insurance enrollees with comprehensive coverage (excluding supplemental coverage enrollees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium adjustment percentage calculation steps and rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the premium adjustment percentage as the ratio of the most recent NHEA projection of per-enrollee premiums for the later year (e.g., 2025) to the NHEA estimate for the base year (2013), with specified rounding steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (1) Calculate per-enrollee private health insurance premiums (excluding Medigap and P&C) for 2013 and 2025; (2) Round each resulting per-enrollee dollar figure to the nearest $1; (3) Divide the 2025 figure by the 2013 figure and carry out the division rounded to 10 significant digits. Example provided: $7,885 (2025) ÷ $4,714 (2013) = 1.6726771319 (proposed PY 2026 premium adjustment percentage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum annual limitation on cost sharing calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For PY 2026, the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing for self-only coverage is the dollar limit for calendar year 2014 increased by the product of that amount and the premium adjustment percentage; for other than self-only coverage, the limit is twice the self-only limit; amounts must be rounded down to the next lowest multiple of $50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 2014 self-only limit $6,350 × proposed premium adjustment percentage 1.6726771319 = proposed PY 2026 self-only limit $10,600; other than self-only = $21,200. HHS will publish these calculated limits in guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing: statutory reductions and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced maximum annual limitations on cost sharing for CSR plan variations are determined per section 1402(c)(1)(A) of the ACA, with the Secretary allowed to adjust them to prevent AVs from exceeding statutory levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS proposes to continue applying reductions as it has since 2015: reduce by 2/3 for enrollees with household income ≥100% and ≤200% FPL; reduce by 1/5 for enrollees with household income >200% and ≤250% FPL; no reduction for >250% and ≤400% FPL for PY 2026. QHP issuers must provide CSRs via plan variations under 45 CFR part 156, subpart E, and ensure annual limitations on cost sharing do not exceed the applicable reduced maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing AV impacts of reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate that the reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing does not cause the actuarial value (AV) of silver-level QHP variations to exceed statutory AV thresholds using model QHPs and the AV Calculator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS tested PY 2026 proposed reduced limits using a set of model plans (typical PPO: $8,850 OOP, $3,250 deductible, 25% coinsurance; PPO with lower OOP: $6,650 OOP, $4,500 deductible, 25% coinsurance; HMO: $8,850 OOP, $3,700 deductible, 25% coinsurance, and specified copays). Use the PY 2026 AV Calculator draft to observe AVs; HHS found the 2/3 reductions would not cause AVs to exceed 94% and 87% thresholds for the lower income bands, but some statutory reductions would cause exceedances for certain bands absent other cost-sharing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contribution percentage calculation (affordability exemption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the required contribution percentage for PY 2026 using the most recent projections and estimates of premium growth and income growth from 2013 to the preceding calendar year (2013 to 2025 for PY 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Income growth measure: NHEA projections of per capita personal income (PI). Steps: (1) compute rate of income growth = PI(2025)/PI(2013) carried to ten significant digits (example 74,083/44,559 = 1.6625821944); (2) compute excess = premium_adjustment_percentage ÷ income_growth (example 1.6726771319 ÷ 1.6625821944 = 1.0060718427); (3) multiply the initial 2014 required contribution percentage (8.00%) by the excess to get the proposed required contribution percentage (example 8.00 × 1.0060718427 = 8.05% rounded to nearest hundredth of 1 percent). The required contribution percentage is used for affordability exemptions (e.g., catastrophic coverage eligibility) despite the individual shared responsibility payment being set to $0 after 2018.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and rulemaking procedure for premium adjustment percentage and related parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will publish the premium adjustment percentage, maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, and required contribution percentage in guidance by January of the year preceding the applicable plan year, unless HHS amends the methodology (in which case parameters will be published through notice-and-comment rulemaking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy (from the 2022 Payment Notice) remains in effect: methodology changes require notice-and-comment, while numerical parameter publication can occur in guidance if the methodology is unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-specific dataset option for AV calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: States are permitted to request HHS approval of State-specific datasets for use as the standard population to calculate actuarial value (AV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must meet the deadlines specified by HHS (for PY 2026, dataset submission deadline was September 1, 2024). If no state dataset is approved/submitted, national standard population will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory alignment: prioritize the ACA statutory objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of the premium measure must align with the ACA directive to base the premium adjustment percentage on 'the average per capita premium for health insurance coverage in the United States' and should not allow other policy objectives to undermine that statutory objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS will consider other policy objectives (e.g., making coverage more affordable) but cautions that accounting for such objectives should not distort the required alignment between premium growth and the parameters subject to the premium adjustment percentage. HHS retains discretion but must faithfully execute statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of downstream market and tax impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: When changing the premium measure or premium adjustment percentage, HHS should consider and describe expected impacts on PTC amounts, required contribution percentages, employer shared responsibility payments, plan design flexibility (e.g., bronze plan AV compliance), and potential enrollment/premiums feedback effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS analysis discusses likely effects: a higher premium adjustment percentage increases maximum annual limitation on cost sharing and required contribution percentage, decreases PTC availability, may reduce Exchange enrollment slightly, could change net premiums and cost-sharing design choices for issuers, and affects Treasury/IRS indexing decisions (Treasury/IRS historically adopt HHS-selected measures for section 36B indexing). Comments are solicited on these anticipated impacts.
